title: Overdue Customer-Funded Draws on Reconstruction Contracts: Grace Period, Charges and Suspension
content:
**Clause 1 — customer-funded draws only.** On Reconstruction contracts, overdue draw charges, suspension and remobilization apply only to customer-funded draws. Carrier-funded and mortgagee-funded draws carry none of them while the funds are pending, because their timing rests with the carrier or the mortgagee.

**Clause 2 — grace period.** An overdue draw charge may post only after the grace period following the draw's due date has fully passed. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the draw's due date, and the first charge may post on the day after the grace period's last day.

**Clauses no longer in force.** The following clauses are no longer in force; each has been superseded by the current overdue charge and suspension basis:

- "The charge is the tier's monthly overdue percentage of the draw's unpaid amount, at most once per draw per calendar month fee period, rounded to the cent, half up." — no longer in force.
- "When a customer-funded draw stays unpaid for more than the tier's stop-work days after its due date, work is suspended; when the draw is paid in full, work resumes and the tier's remobilization fee is booked once for that resumption." — no longer in force.

## Judging clause 1

The draw's funding route on the draw record decides: a draw whose route is the customer can carry an overdue draw charge and can lead to suspension; a carrier-direct or mortgagee-release draw carries neither while its funds are pending.

## Judging clause 2

- The clock starts from the due date on the draw record; the due date itself is not counted.
- The grace days are counted as calendar days from the day after the due date.
- The first day a charge may post is the day after the last grace day; on the last grace day itself no charge may post.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, on an agreement with a 5-day grace).** A draw due on the 10th of a month: grace days are the 11th to the 15th. No charge may post on the 15th; the first charge may post on the 16th.

| Day (draw due on the 10th, 5-day grace) | Overdue draw charge may post |
|---|---|
| 15th (last grace day) | No |
| 16th | Yes |

superseded_clauses: The charge is the tier's monthly overdue percentage of the draw's unpaid amount, at most once per draw per calendar month fee period, rounded to the cent, half up.

When a customer-funded draw stays unpaid for more than the tier's stop-work days after its due date, work is suspended; when the draw is paid in full, work resumes and the tier's remobilization fee is booked once for that resumption.
